Reasons for Submitting the Bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this Bill is to introduce a sound legal basis setting out the principles and procedures relating to the determination of the death penalty upon persons in the Maldives and the enforcement of the penalty, having regard to the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the principles of international law, and the rights of the general public and of the convicted person. Accordingly, this Bill determines the conditions that must be fulfilled for the death penalty to be determined upon persons in the Maldives and the principles that courts must follow in determining the penalty; sets out the procedures that must be completed in sequence for the enforcement of the death penalty, the rights of the person upon whom the death penalty has been determined, and the circumstances and reasons for which the enforcement of the penalty shall be postponed; and finally, sets out the principles and procedures relating to the determination of the death penalty and the enforcement of the penalty.

Bill on the Determination of the Death Penalty and the Enforcement of the Penalty

Chapter One
Preliminary

Introduction and title
1. (a) This is the Act that determines the conditions that must be fulfilled for the death penalty to be determined upon persons in the Maldives and the principles that courts must follow in determining the penalty, and sets out the procedures that must be completed in sequence for the enforcement of the death penalty, the rights to be afforded to the person upon whom the death penalty has been determined, the circumstances and reasons for which the enforcement of the penalty shall be postponed, and finally, the principles and procedures relating to the determination of the death penalty and the enforcement of the penalty.

(b) This Act shall be cited as the "Death Penalty Determination and Enforcement Act".

Purpose
2. The purpose of this Act is to achieve the following:

(a) to determine the conditions that must be fulfilled for the death penalty to be determined upon a person, where a court of the Maldives has proven upon that person an offence for which the death penalty may be determined;

[stamp] [signature]

the penalty carried out where, at the trial of a criminal case conducted in a court of the Maldives, the offence is proven against the party accused of the offence, and the court sentences that person to be put to death as a penalty for that offence.

Chapter Two
Conditions for Determining the Death Penalty

Not determining the penalty unless the conditions for the death penalty are fulfilled
5. No court of the Maldives shall determine the death penalty upon any person unless all the conditions set out in this Chapter are fulfilled, and only in accordance with the procedures set out in this Chapter.

Determination of the penalty by law
6. (a) In determining the death penalty upon the convicted person, in addition to the offence proven against that person being determined and set out as a hadd offence in Law No. 9/2014 (Penal Code of the Maldives) or in another Act specifically designated for determining criminal offences and penalties, it must be stated in that Act that the penalty for that offence, or a penalty among the penalties for it, is the death penalty.

(b) The condition set out in subsection (a) of this Article must have been fulfilled in that court from the time the convicted person committed the offence until the sentence determining the death penalty upon that person is passed.

Hearing of the case at all stages of trial
7. (a) Even where a lower court has sentenced the convicted person to death as a penalty for the offence, all the legal points of that sentence and the facts of the case shall be

[stamp] [signature]

reviewed anew by the superior courts of the Maldives.

(b) Even where neither the State nor the convicted person submits the case for appeal to a superior court, the superior courts shall hear that case as an appeal case in the manner set out in subsection (a) of this Article.

(c) A sentence determining the death penalty shall become a final sentence only when, after the Supreme Court has heard that case, that Court determines the death penalty upon the convicted person.

Conducting trials with justice and fairness
8. (a) The death penalty shall be determined upon the convicted person only after a trial conducted with fairness and justice, impartially and equitably, at a hearing held open to the public, within a reasonable period, in an independent and [unclear] court guaranteed by law.

(b) Before the Supreme Court determines the death penalty upon the convicted person, that Court shall ensure that the stages of trial have been conducted in the manner set out in subsection (a) of this Article.

(c) The Supreme Court shall examine whether the matters set out in subsection (a) of this Article have been fulfilled to a standard higher than the standard at which such matters are ordinarily examined, and [unclear] at every stage of the trial.

[stamp] [signature]

(d) In examining whether the matters set out in subsection (a) of this Article have been fulfilled, the Supreme Court shall examine them in a manner that includes the following fundamental matters:

(1) that the right set out in Article 42 of the Constitution has been afforded to the convicted person;

(2) that the right set out in Article 51 of the Constitution has been afforded to the convicted person;

(3) that the right set out in Article 56 of the Constitution has been afforded to the convicted person.

(e) If, after examining the matters required to be examined under this Article, the court is satisfied that those matters have not been fulfilled, the death penalty shall not be determined for the offence proven against the convicted person.

Right to obtain the assistance of a legal counsel
9. (a) The right to seek and obtain the assistance of a legal counsel must have been fully afforded to the convicted person at all of the following stages:

(1) at the stage of investigation of the offence; and

(2) in submitting an appeal of the sentence to the courts of higher instance; and

(3) at all stages of the trial.

[stamp] [signature]

(b) Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this Article, where the right to seek and obtain the assistance of a legal counsel is withheld upon a determination made under the authority of law and in accordance with law, or where the convicted person waives that right of their own free choice, seeking the assistance of a legal counsel and that assistance shall not be deemed [unclear] the opportunity for defence.

(c) Before determining the death penalty upon the convicted person, the court shall ensure that the right to seek and obtain the assistance of a legal counsel has been afforded to the convicted person in the manner set out in this Article.

(d) If, after examining the matters required to be examined under this Article, the court is satisfied that the right to seek and obtain the assistance of a legal counsel has not been afforded to the convicted person, the death penalty shall not be determined for the offence proven against the convicted person.

Agreement of the heirs
10. (a) Where the charge brought against the convicted person is a charge of the offence of killing a person, for the purpose of determining the death penalty upon the convicted person, it must be stated in the trial of that case that all the heirs of the person killed wish to exact qisas from the convicted person.

(b) The decision made at the trial stage by all the heirs of the person killed, wishing to exact qisas from the convicted person, must remain in effect in that court until the court determines the death penalty upon the convicted person.

[stamp] [signature]

(c) Even where the heirs of the person killed have decided at an earlier stage of the trial to exact qisas from the convicted person, if, before the penalty is determined upon the convicted person, any heir among the heirs of the person killed informs the court that they do not wish to exact qisas from that person, the court shall ascertain that matter before determining the penalty.

(d) Where all the heirs of the person killed do not wish to exact qisas from the convicted person, the death penalty shall not be determined for that offence.

(e) For the purposes of this Article, only those heirs among the heirs of the convicted person who have attained the age of 15 (fifteen) years shall be deemed to be heirs.

Withdrawal of the decision of the heirs
25. (a) Where the case in which the death penalty has been determined upon the convicted person is a case of killing a person,

even where it is stated in the trial of that case that all the heirs of the person killed wish to exact diyat from the convicted person, any heir among the heirs of the person killed may withdraw that decision until the commencement of the enforcement of the death penalty under Article 39 of this Act.

(b) Where any heir among the heirs of the person killed wishes to withdraw the decision to exact diyat and change that decision, that heir may submit that matter to the Supreme Court.

(c) Where a submission is made in any form to the Supreme Court under subsection (b) of this Article, the Supreme Court shall decide to postpone the enforcement of the death penalty.

(d) In examining and deciding on a submission made to the Supreme Court under this Article, that Court shall ascertain with certainty that there is an heir among the heirs of the person killed who wishes to exact diyat from the convicted person.

(e) Where, upon examining a submission made to the Supreme Court under this Article, the Supreme Court ascertains with certainty that any heir among the heirs of the person killed wishes to exact diyat from the convicted person, the Supreme Court shall annul the death penalty previously determined by the Supreme Court upon the convicted person, and shall transfer that case to the court of first instance for the determination of a different penalty that may be determined for that offence under the Act under which the charge was brought against the convicted person.

Chapter Six
Enforcement of the Death Penalty

Office enforcing the penalty
32. All matters of the practical enforcement of the death penalty upon the convicted person shall be carried out by the Maldives Correctional Service.

Means of enforcing the penalty
33. (a) The death penalty shall be enforced upon the convicted person under this Act by hanging that person.

(b) For the purposes of subsection (a) of this Article, hanging means, for the purpose of taking the life of the convicted person, after placing a rope around that person's neck, [unclear] causing that person to be suspended by that rope.

(c) The instruments and items used to enforce the death penalty by hanging, and the manner in which it is carried out, shall be instruments, items and a manner by which the penalty can be enforced in a way that causes the least pain to the convicted person and as quickly as possible. Accordingly, the party enforcing the penalty shall ensure the fundamental matters.

(1) that the instruments used in hanging are instruments suitable for that purpose;

(2) that the manner of hanging is a manner by which the life of the convicted person

can be taken most quickly;

(3) that the manner of hanging is a manner by which life can be taken with little pain;

(4) that the persons involved in the hanging are persons who have received [unclear] training.

(d) The items and instruments used in hanging, and the detailed principles and procedures of hanging, shall be set out in the regulation made under this Act, in accordance with the standards set out in subsection (c) of this Article.

(e) The persons involved in hanging the convicted person shall be officers of the Maldives Correctional Service determined by that Service.

Inspection of the arrangements made for enforcing the penalty
36. (a) Upon completion of the arrangements for enforcing the death penalty in the manner set out in Article 34 of this Act, the Commissioner of Prisons shall inform the Judge set out in Article 17 of this Act of that matter.

(c) Where, after examining under subsection (b) of this Article the manner in which the arrangements for enforcing the death penalty have been made, the Judge finds that there is a matter requiring rectification, the Judge shall instruct the Commissioner of Prisons to rectify that matter within a maximum of 48 (forty-eight) hours.

Authorisation to enforce the death penalty
37. (a) The death penalty determined upon the convicted person shall be practically enforced under this Act only upon the Judges set out in Article 17 of this Act giving the Maldives Correctional Service authorisation to enforce the penalty.

(b) The Judges shall give the Maldives Correctional Service authorisation to enforce the death penalty in writing. Furthermore, the document of that authorisation shall be prepared in accordance with the template set out in the regulation

made under this Act.

(c) The Judges shall give authorisation to enforce the death penalty only after examining and ascertaining the following matters.

(1) ascertaining with certainty that no reason or circumstance exists under Article 12 of this Act for which the enforcement of the death penalty must be postponed;

(2) that all the arrangements required to be made under this Chapter for the enforcement of the death penalty have been made in the manner set out in this Chapter.

(d) In the Judges' examination of the matters set out in subsection (c)(1) of this Article, the decision on that matter shall be made in accordance with the principles set out in Article 24 of this Act.

(e) Where, in the Judges' examination of the matters set out in subsection (c)(2) of this Article, the Judges find that those matters have not been arranged, or have not been arranged in accordance with this Act, they shall decide to postpone the enforcement of the death penalty until those arrangements are made, and shall inform the parties set out in Article 23(c) of this Act of that matter.

(f) Where, after examining the matters required to be examined by the Judges under subsection (c)(1) and (2) of this Article, the Judges find that there is no reason obstructing the enforcement of the death penalty, they shall issue the document authorising the enforcement of the penalty and send it to the Commissioner of Prisons.

(g) Even where the Judges have previously carried out and completed the procedures set out in this Article, if the date and time for enforcing the death penalty are determined and changed, the procedures set out in this Article shall be carried out and completed anew.

(h) Upon the Commissioner of Prisons receiving the document authorising the enforcement of the death penalty, the Commissioner shall immediately inform the parties set out in Article 23(c) of this Act of that matter, and shall send those parties a copy of the authorisation document received.

(i) Where, after authorisation to enforce the penalty has been given under this Article and before the enforcement of the penalty commences under Article 39 of this Act, any circumstance arises under this Act for which the enforcement of the penalty must be postponed, the Judges shall instruct that the enforcement of the penalty be postponed.

Preparing to enforce the death penalty
38. (a) Upon the Judges giving authorisation to enforce the death penalty under Article 37 of this Act, the procedures set out in this Article shall be carried out and completed by way of preparing to enforce the penalty.

(b) Before the convicted person is brought to the place where the penalty is to be enforced, the Commissioner of Prisons shall ensure that the parties required to be present at the place where the death penalty is enforced under Article 35 of this Act, and the parties having the right to be present at that place, are present.

(c) Before the convicted person is brought to the place where the penalty is to be enforced, suitable arrangements shall be made for that person to perform worship, and the opportunity to do so shall be given. Furthermore, where the convicted person is a Muslim, before the convicted person is brought to the place where the penalty is to be enforced, that person shall be given the opportunity to pray, if that person so wishes.

(d) Before the penalty is enforced upon the convicted person, after that person is brought to the place, that person shall be kept in a place where they are to stay, and, before the procedures for enforcing the penalty commence, the matters and policy to be carried out shall be explained [unclear], the first procedure shall be explained, and that person shall be given the opportunity to prepare.

(e) After the opportunity is communicated under subsection (d) of this Article, and after the opportunity to prepare for the enforcement of the penalty is given, the penalty shall be enforced in the manner set out in Article 39 of this Act.

Enforcement of the death penalty
39. (a) After the Judges give authorisation to enforce the death penalty under Article 37 of this Act, and after the procedures required to take place before the enforcement of the death penalty under Article 38 of this Act are completed, the death penalty shall be enforced upon the convicted person in accordance with this Article.

(b) For the purposes of subsection (a) of this Article, commencing the enforcement of the death penalty means, after placing a rope around the neck of the convicted person by way of hanging that person in the manner set out in Article 33 of this Act, suspending that person by that rope.

(f) acting contrary to respect for the body of the deceased.

Inability to enforce the penalty
42. (a) Even where the enforcement of the penalty has commenced under Article 39 of this Act, if for any reason the penalty cannot be enforced, the enforcement of the penalty shall be stopped.

(b) For the purposes of subsection (a) of this Article, inability to enforce the penalty means the penalty not being able to be enforced because, after placing a rope around the neck of the convicted person for hanging and suspending that person by that rope, [unclear] that person's life does not depart, or because of a defect in an instrument or item used for hanging, or for any other reason.

(c) Where the enforcement of the penalty is stopped under this Article, that fact shall be immediately communicated to the Judge set out in Article 17 of this Act.

(d) Where the enforcement of the penalty is stopped under this Article, the matters of enforcing the penalty may be proceeded with further only after a date for enforcing the penalty is determined anew under Article 23 of this Act and the procedures required to be completed under this Act are completed anew.

Communicating the news that the death penalty has been enforced
43. (a) Upon the death penalty being enforced under Article 39 of this Act, that fact shall be communicated to the Judge set out in Article 17 of this Act.

(b) When, upon the enforcement of the death penalty, that fact is communicated to the Judge under subsection (a) of this Article, it shall be in a document specified by the Judge.

Chapter Seven
Miscellaneous

Transitional matters
44. (a) Upon the commencement of this Act, sentences determining the death penalty that have become final in the manner set out in Article 7 of this Act shall, for the purposes of Article 5 of this Act, be deemed to be penalties determined in fulfilment of the Parts set out in Chapter Two of this Act and in accordance with the principles and procedures set out in that Chapter.

(b) Upon the commencement of this Act, where a sentence pronouncing the death penalty has become final in the manner set out in Article 7 of this Act and the period set out in Article 16 of this Act has been completed, the procedures of the Chapter of this Act in relation to such penalties shall commence within 3 (three) months of the commencement of this Act.

Keeping in custody in lieu of the death penalty not being enforced, and conversion to the penalty that went for enforcement
45. (a) Upon the death penalty being determined upon the convicted person, that person shall be detained in prison until that penalty is enforced under this Act. During that period, that person shall be held in custody in a special place, separately from other inmates. Furthermore, during that period, that person shall be held in accordance with the principles for enforcing the penalty of imprisonment.

(b) Where it is determined that the death penalty determined upon the convicted person is not a penalty that may be enforced under this Act, then, for the determination of a different penalty that may be determined for that offence under the Act under which the charge was brought against that person, the case shall be submitted for the matter of determining the penalty to be commenced to be heard [unclear] the court of first instance.

Not being affected by the expiry of time limits
46. (a) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary stated in any other Act, even after the death sentence pronounced upon a person has become final, where evidence is obtained that would exonerate that person of the offence proven against them, or evidence indicating testimony such that the penalty for that offence would have to be reduced, or information such as may give rise to doubt as to the integrity and validity of the evidence used in proving the offence against that person, a case may be submitted to the Supreme Court for that case to be heard anew.

(b) A case such as that set out in this Article may be submitted at any time, even where the sentence pronouncing the death penalty has become final, until that sentence is enforced under this Act.

(c) Where a case set out in this Article is submitted to the Supreme Court, the acts of enforcing the death penalty shall be halted until that Court makes a decision in that case.

(d) Where a case such as that set out in this Article is submitted to the Supreme Court, no procedure for enforcing the death penalty under this Act shall be carried out until that Court hears and decides that case.

Counting of periods
48. Unless otherwise specifically stated in this Act, the periods set out in this Act shall be counted inclusive of public holidays.

Making regulations
49. (a) In addition to the regulations which this Act specifically states are to be made by the Supreme Court, the regulations required to be made under this Act for the implementation of this Act shall be made and administered by the Maldives Correctional Service.
